p: after the uproar was ceased: Paul departs from Ephesus by the consent of the church, not to be idle or at rest, but to take pains in another place.
much exhortation: For after so great trouble, there was need of much exhortation.
And there abode three months: A perverse zeal is the guider and instructor to murderers: and we are not excluded by the wisdom of God to prevent the endeavours of wicked men.
And upon the: Assemblies in the night-time cannot be justly condemned, neither should they be, when the cause is good.

first day of the week: Literally, "the first day of the Sabbath", that is, upon the Lord's day: so that by this place, and by 1Co 16:2 we properly understand that in those days the Christians habitually assembled themselves solemnly together upon that day.
And there were many lights in: The devil, taking care to trouble the Church with a great offence, gives Paul a singular occasion to confirm the Gospel

For Paul had determined to sail: Paul, an earnest and diligent follower of Christ, making haste to his bonds without any ceasing or stopping in his race, first of all as it were makes his testament, wherein he gives an account of his former life, defends the doctrine which he taught, and exhorts the pastors of the church to persevere and go forward with continuance in their office.
Miletus he sent to Ephesus: According as the situation of these places is set forth, the distance between Ephesus and Miletus was almost 50 miles or 80 km.
And when they were come to: A graphic image of a true pastor.
back nothing that was profitable unto: I did not refrain form speaking, neither did I conceal my motives in any way at all, either for fear or for wicked gain.
And now: He testifies that he goes to his imprisonment by the commandment of God.
bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem: He calls the guiding direction of the Holy Spirit, who forced him to take his journey to Jerusalem, the bond of the Sprit, whom he followed with all his heart.
pure from the blood of all: If you perish, yet there will fault with me. See Geneva
For I have not shunned to: The doctrine of the apostles is most perfect and absolute.
feed the church of God: To keep it, to feed and govern it.

he hath purchased with: A notable sentence for Christ's Godhead: which shows plainly in his person, how that by reason of the joining together of the two natures in his own person, that which is proper to one is spoken of the other, being taken as deriving from one another, and not in the original: which in old time the godly fathers termed a communicating or fellowship of properties or attributes, that is to say, a making common of that to two, which belongs but to one.
his own blood: The words "his own" show forth the excellency of that blood.
For I know this: A prophecy of pastors that would immediately degenerate into wolves, against those who boast and brag only of a succession of persons.
draw away disciples after them: This is great misery, to want the presence of such a shepherd, but it is a greater misery to have wolves enter in.
And now: The power of God, and his free promises revealed in his word, are the props and upholders of the ministry of the Gospel.
inheritance among all them which are: As children, and therefore an inheritance of free love and good will.
I have coveted no man's silver: Pastors must before all things beware of covetousness.
to support the weak: As it were by reaching out the hand to those who otherwise are about to slip and fall away, and so to steady them.
And they all wept sore: The Gospel does not take away natural affections, but rules and bridles them in good order.
